Tests for {@link TriDiagonalTransformer}, which decomposes a symmetric matrix A into A = Q × T × Q<sup>T</sup>, where Q is orthogonal and T is symmetric and tridiagonal.
Tolerance for reconstructing the original matrix from Q, T and Q^T.
Tolerance for checking that Q (or Q^T) is orthogonal.
Tolerance for checking that off-tridiagonal entries of T are zero.
Tolerance for comparing Q and T against known reference values.
expected: the transformer only accepts square matrices
Asserts that Q × T × Q^T reproduces the original matrix.
Verifies that the transformer never reads entries strictly below the diagonal: poisoning them with NaN must not affect the decomposition, which should still reconstruct the original (clean) matrix.
Replace every entry below the diagonal in this row with NaN.
Asserts that the given matrix is orthogonal, i.e. m^T × m = I.
Asserts that every entry outside the main diagonal and its two adjacent diagonals is zero, as required for a tridiagonal matrix.

Checks Q and T against precomputed reference values, and verifies that repeated getter calls return the same cached instances. @param matrix input matrix to transform @param expectedQ expected orthogonal matrix Q @param mainDiagonal expected main diagonal of T @param secondaryDiagonal expected sub-/super-diagonal of T
Q must match the known reference matrix.
Rebuild the expected tridiagonal T from its two diagonals.
The getters must return the same cached instance on subsequent calls.
